name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=paint/gfx, descriptor=char_sprite_at_world_pos). No address residue. Accurately reflects the body: paints one runtime_char's facing sprite at its battle-world position into the render workspace, applying chapter palette, sleep-status shake jitter, and a greyed look once the unit has acted. Callers (fd2_composite_all_chars_overlay, death/dialog/spell animators) all pass a runtime-char index, confirming the per-char paint semantics.
purpose: Paint one runtime_char's facing sprite at its battle-world position into the render workspace, applying chapter palette, sleep-status shake jitter, and a greyed-out look once the unit has acted this turn.
logic_summary: If the BIOS tick (signed word @0x46C) changed since last paint, flip the 1-bit shake jitter and latch the new tick. Read the char's (pos_x,pos_y) and facing=sprite_state[1]; return if outside the visible window (origin +/- max, with +/-1 tile margins). Pick a per-facing pitch delta (down +0x720, left -4, up -0x720, right +4) and compute blit_offset = walk_phase(sprite_state[2])*pitch_delta + (pos_y-origin_y)*0x2AC0 + (pos_x-origin_x)*0x18, adding the shake byte when sleeping. Choose palette: walk_phase==0 -> ambient palette idx else alt palette idx; fold 3 -> 1; sleep forces 0. Look up the sprite via data_fd2_portrait_sprite_cache at index facing*3 + sprite_state[0]*0xC + palette_idx (table of 4-byte relative offsets). Add 0x75D8 (char-layer base); if non-negative, blit the 24x24 tile into large_game_state_buffer+blit_offset with stride 0x1C8 using the dimmed/grayscale blitter when flags bit7 (acted) is set, else the passthrough blitter.

params.name: char_idx
params.semantics: Index into data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr (party/combatant slot) selecting which runtime_char's sprite to paint. Callers pass party-loop indices or a char index from fd2_find_char_at_cursor_pos.
params.reason: Source declaration already names it char_idx, which accurately reflects its use as the runtime_char array index. No address residue. (Ghidra's decompile shows param_1, but the C source uses the proper name.)

returns.semantics: No return value; side effect is blitting the char sprite into the render workspace (or returning early when off-window or when the computed offset is negative).
